title: Semialgebraic universal covers of normal projective varieties
main_claim: Kollár–Pardon conjecture: for a connected normal projective complex variety X, the universal cover is biholomorphic to a semialgebraic open subset of a projective variety iff it is isomorphic to D × C^m × F, where D is a bounded symmetric domain and F is a simply connected normal projective variety. No algebraicity of the deck transformations is assumed.

issues.location: groups.tex, eq. (grp:abelianity-input); used in Lemma grp:countable-core-level, Lemma grp:compactifiable-cover, Theorem grp:kernel-abelian
issues.description: This is an external dependency, not an error. The main theorem rests on the companion OpenAI paper's Theorem 1.1: the full fundamental group of a smooth special compact Kähler manifold is virtually abelian. That is Campana's abelianity conjecture, a major open problem, and its proof is not in this paper. If the companion paper fails, discreteness of the transverse action and virtual abelianity of the fibre kernel both fail, and so does the classification. The dependency is not circular: the companion paper is applied only to smooth compact special core fibres.
issues.evidence: "The group-theoretic input is the theorem of OpenAI that the entire ordinary fundamental group of a connected smooth special compact Kähler manifold is virtually abelian ... That theorem is proved in the separately cited companion article."

issues.description: This corollary is not part of the main theorem. It applies Claudon–Höring–Kollár under their abundance premise and supplies that premise from another unrefereed companion paper (OpenAILogAbundance2026, Theorem 1.1). So it is conditional on that companion paper.

coverage: Read in full and checked step by step: main.tex (introduction, assembly, and the Remmert and Singer corollaries), groups.tex (Liouville lemma, the finite-level projection lemma, countable/locally finite core levels, discreteness via the H^0 orbit argument, the Selberg free finite-index subgroup with stabilizer triviality from the spanning vector fields, the Nadel–Frankel/de Rham step, the compactifiable-cover index argument, kernel abelianity), compact.tex (characteristic subgroup, relative Albanese descent, Kollár–Pardon bundle theorem applied to the Albanese map, fibrewise flatness, affine-bundle triviality via Theorem B and the Oka principle, the controlled proper-homotopy rigidity lemma, Chow homeomorphism T≅C, the integral-marking polarized locus with c1 injective on simply connected normal F, the density argument, Hilbert/Douady local triviality, the converse), quotient.tex (pseudoconvexity, the tower lemma, guards, the incidence/trace lemma, descent and normal-fibre preparation, the intrinsic projection theorem), windows.tex (plaques, period matrix, seed Bergman lemma, exact first epigraph, the window theorem statement, tower properties) and quasiprojective.tex. Verified by hand: the Siegel/Cayley identity Im S−|W|^2 = Im s − (Im w)^T A Im w; the guard sector and decay bounds; the bounded-realization inversion formulas w = Db/(ia) and s = i(1−a+i w^T b)/a; triangularity of the spanning orbit fields. Only skimmed, not line-checked: preliminaries.tex (Puiseux preparation, finite-jet specialization, hole trapping, thin pseudoconcave analyticity, projective-fibre propagation), most of localization.tex (attached discs, upper containment), and the inductive body of the win:construction proof. These are the deepest analytic parts and are where an undetected gap would most likely be.
